You are a senior software engineer on the Node.js core team. The Technical Steering Committee (TSC) has asked you to write a design document for the decision to unflag the `--experimental-strip-types` flag, making TypeScript type-stripping enabled by default in Node.js. This document will serve as the architectural record for the change and will be shared with the broader ecosystem to explain the rationale, scope, and implications.

You have been provided with the PR #56350 diff and description, which shows the actual code and documentation changes made to the nodejs/node repository. Your task is to synthesize this information into a structured design document.

The document should cover the following:

1. **Overview**: Explain the change in plain terms—what is being unflagged, what it means for users, and why this is being done now (referencing the PR author's stated rationale).

2. **Motivation and Context**: Describe the motivation behind enabling TypeScript support by default. Reference the linked issue from the nodejs/typescript repository (issue #17) as the motivating bug. Discuss the experimental nature of the feature and its stability classification (1.1 - Active development).

What it means for Node.js users

paragraphs: PR #56350 enables the `--experimental-strip-types` flag by default in Node.js. Previously, users had to explicitly pass `--experimental-strip-types` to run TypeScript files. With this change, Node.js can execute TypeScript files containing inline type annotations without any additional configuration.

The PR author's rationale is that it is time to enable the feature by default to catch more bugs, noting that currently there are no open issues. By exposing the feature to a wider user base by default, the team can identify edge cases and regressions more effectively before the feature is eventually stabilized.
Users who do not wish to use this feature can opt out by passing the new `--no-experimental-strip-types` flag.

required_content: Reference to nodejs/typescript issue #17 as the motivating bug
Mention of the feature's experimental status and stability classification (1.1 - Active development)
paragraphs: This change is motivated by the need to move the TypeScript type-stripping feature toward broader adoption. The PR fixes issue #17 in the nodejs/typescript repository, which tracked the goal of enabling the feature by default.

The feature retains its experimental classification (Stability: 1.1 - Active development). This means it remains subject to change, but is considered stable enough for default enablement. The documentation notes that TypeScript type-stripping is experimental and users should be aware of its limitations.

required_content: Changes to benchmark/ts/strip-typescript.js: removal of --experimental-strip-types flag from the flags array
Removal of the --experimental-strip-types section from doc/api/cli.md

Updates to --input-type description removing the flag requirement
paragraphs: The changes span 22 files with 64 additions and 114 deletions. The key modifications are as follows:

In `benchmark/ts/strip-typescript.js`, the `flags` array was changed from `['--experimental-strip-types', '--disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning']` to `['--disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning']`. This reflects that the benchmark no longer needs to explicitly enable the flag since it is now on by default.

In `doc/api/cli.md`, the existing section documenting `--experimental-strip-types` was removed entirely. In its place, a new section for `--no-experimental-strip-types` was added, allowing users to disable the default behavior. The YAML metadata for the new section references `added: v22.6.0` with a changes entry for the version when it was unflagged.

The `--entry-url` example was updated. Previously it showed `node --entry-url --experimental-strip-types 'file.ts?query#hash'`; it now shows `node --entry-url 'file.ts?query#hash'`, removing the explicit flag.

The `--input-type` description was updated. The sentence stating that the `"-typescript"` values are available only in combination with `--experimental-strip-types` was changed to state that they are not available with `--no-experimental-strip-types`. The conditional about `--experimental-strip-types` being enabled and `--input-type` not being provided was also simplified.

The `--experimental-typescript-transform` description was updated to remove the statement that it implies `--experimental-strip-types`, since that flag is no longer a separate opt-in. It now only implies `--enable-source-maps`.

md_sections.heading: Semver Classification
required_content: PR author's statement that this is a semver minor change
Explanation of why this classification is appropriate
paragraphs: The PR author classifies this change as semver minor. This classification is appropriate because the change enables new functionality by default without breaking existing behavior for users who were not previously opting in.

Users who were already passing `--experimental-strip-types` will see no change in behavior—their TypeScript files continue to work. Users who were not passing the flag and not using TypeScript will also see no change. The only new behavior is that users who run `.ts` files without the flag will now have them executed, which is additive functionality.

md_sections.heading: Limitations and Future Work
required_content: Statement that the feature remains experimental and subject to change
paragraphs: The feature has documented limitations in supported TypeScript syntax, detailed at https://nodejs.org/api/typescript.html#type-stripping. Users and library authors should consult this documentation to understand what TypeScript constructs are supported by the type-stripping approach.

As noted in the PR description, this feature is experimental and is subject to change. The TSC and core team will continue to monitor for issues and regressions now that the feature is enabled by default. Future work may include expanding supported syntax, improving performance, and eventually stabilizing the feature.
